_note: THE MILITARY FAMILY, 4 OF ~10: THE UPLINK.

THE HOOK (10-28): the records are the garrison's unsent mail, and the radio is someone who wrote one. Rewritten 2026-10-28 on his bar, "just about making each mission feel interesting in some way" (and "go ahead on the 7"): the draft had nothing in it worth mentioning afterwards.
Start the site's uplink from its own terminal, then hold the room while it sends. The verb is HOLD: the first of the
family where you stay put. Waves defend the terminal (a hold's defend). Rung 1 squads, rung 3 a horde.
Written to the delve marker set (outside entrance, centre, item markers, boss, wounded) on his ruling, so the
lint pool is EMPTY on military sites until the markers are on them (missionboard06a's note says why).
Every word holds at any military site: nothing names the site, the faction or the weather; everything the lines
point at is placed. Pay: med, capped.

place._theme: Military sites; the family's marker set.

prose.name: Defense: Unsent Letters on <Planet>
prose.briefing: The <Place> fell with its outbound mail still queued on the site terminal. The terminal can still send it, slowly, if someone holds the site.
prose.card: Local Contract. Hold the <Place> on <Planet> while its terminal sends the unsent mail. Payment on contract completion.

beats.journal: The uplink is running. The queue is four hundred and twelve letters long and it sends them one at a time. Something in the <Place> has noticed, and I need to hold the room.
beats.name: Site Uplink Terminal
say: It's sending. I can see them landing at this end, one at a time. Keep whatever comes for that terminal off it.

beats.journal: I held the room until the last letter went.
say: That's the queue empty. Mine was in there, near the bottom. I wrote it the night before they came in, and I can't remember a word of what I said.

broadcast: When we lost the place, the outbound mail was still sitting in that terminal, every letter anyone wrote that month. Start the uplink and stay with it, because it's slow and it's loud and they'll come to see what's talking.
_speech: On a board the broadcast waits for him at the site. Not yet heard in game; his ear decides. No names, places, factions or currency in a voiced line.
